findings.title: Index updates can be lost during startup rebuild
findings.body: The search watcher is subscribed only after all namespace indexes have been built from point-in-time ListIterator scans. Writes made after a namespace has been scanned and before WatchWriteEvents is opened are not included in that namespace's rebuilt index, and the SQL watch implementation starts from the latest revision when it subscribes, so it will not replay that gap. In HA deployments, writes from another server during a potentially long startup build will therefore leave search results permanently stale until each affected object is modified again. Subscribe/buffer before taking rebuild snapshots, or replay events from each build's returned resource version before publishing the index.

findings.title: TotalDocs ranges over the cache without synchronization
findings.body: BuildIndex now permits concurrent index construction and mutates b.cache under cacheMu at lines 137-139, while TotalDocs iterates the same map without even an RLock. A concurrent TotalDocs call can race with the assignment and can terminate the process with Go's "concurrent map iteration and map write" panic (as well as producing a race-detector failure). Hold cacheMu.RLock for the entire iteration, or iterate over a protected snapshot.

findings.title: Bleve build span context is still discarded
findings.body: BuildIndex starts a tracing span but assigns its returned context to `_`, so the builder callback and any work it invokes continue using the parent context rather than the Bleve BuildIndex span. This leaves the newly added BuildIndex span without the expected descendant storage/build spans and does not satisfy the stated trace-context propagation goal. Assign the returned context and pass it to downstream work (which may require the builder callback contract to accept a context).
